d: The British School of Bahrain is committed to providing a high-quality, international education for students in the Kingdom of Bahrain. We are a selective, coeducational, independent Nursery-through-Year 13 school. Our curriculum is based on the National Curriculum for England and Wales, with some adaptations to the local context and offers IGCSE and A-Level/BTEC examinations. While the language of academic instruction is English, we are a truly international school, and our pupils and staff come from over 82 different nationalities. The school has 2600 students on roll aged 3-18, it has a warm feel to it, and there is a sense of fun. Most importantly, our students are a joy to teach.

Judged as ‘Outstanding’ in both our most recent BSO and BQA inspections, we have high expectations of our students throughout their educational journey. Our aim is to provide our graduating students with a passport to the best universities, colleges and careers around the world.
We are welcoming applications for a Bahraini Teaching Assistant - Infant School to join us in November 2026.
q: Experience in dealing with children in Infant school.
Ability to work effectively both as part of a team and also independently.
Ability to work collaboratively and supportively with colleagues within the school and parents.
Ability to manage commitments and deadlines.
Commitment to continuing personal and professional development.
Demonstrated commitment to the highest standards of accuracy, attention to detail, and handling of confidential information.
Demonstrated knowledge and experience with the use of ICT in teaching and learning support.
Bachelor’s degree or relevant higher-level qualification or vocational training that can be practically applied to supporting pupil development.
Minimum 3 years’ teaching and learning support experience in Education sector.

Inspired Education Group is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expects all staff, volunteers and other third parties to share this commitment. Safer recruitment practices and pre-employment background checks will be undertaken before any appointment is confirmed.
r: Support pupils during lessons as directed by the class teacher
Supervise and teach individual, pairs or groups of children as required by the class teacher or line manager
Be aware of the teacher’s weekly planning and be ready to assist with lesson preparation by preparing resources (Note. Preparation of ILN resources required by the TA will take priority).
Display pupils’ work as requested and remove when necessary
Supervise pupils in the communal areas to ensure a high standard of behaviour is maintained.
Provide duty cover for absent colleagues when requested to do so by a line manager
Reward and sanction children in accordance with the school’s ‘Positive Behaviour’ policy to ensure the school’s high standards of behaviour and discipline are maintained.
Act as a role model for pupils
To promote the school positively at all times
To work with colleagues in a spirit of mutual cooperation to maintain and enhance a pleasant professional working environment
Refer comments, questions and complaints from parents directly to the class teacher.
Be available for regular, weekly meetings with the class teacher
To undertake any other reasonable task as instructed by the Head of Infant School or any other line manager.
